clue.text: Stopped, in Titanic, putting time into small movie part

indicators.note: putting one thing into another tells us the time letter goes inside the movie part

parts.note: a cameo is a brief walk-on role in a film

explanation.surface: Someone explains a scene in the film Titanic where a star's brief walk-on gets more screen time.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship 'comes to' when it is brought to a halt, so the nautical phrase suits the Titanic setting.
explanation.definitionFit: In seafaring language a vessel that halts has been brought up, so the ship is said to have come to.

clue.text: Chicago star in costume, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word for costume is to be pronounced, giving a name that sounds the same

parts.note: gear is clothing or costume

explanation.surface: An actor from the musical film Chicago appears dressed in costume.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Gere played the lawyer Billy Flynn in the 2002 film Chicago; 'Chicago' is the film, not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Gere was a leading actor in the film musical Chicago.

clue.text: Like stars from ET set, all confused

indicators.note: confused means the letters of these three words are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: Something star-like springs from a film set for ET, everyone bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges the letters of ET SET ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellate is a botanical and zoological adjective for something radiating in a star shape.

clue.text: Strangely normal name for best actor twice

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the next word are arranged in an odd new order

explanation.surface: An ordinary forename turns out to belong to a double Oscar-winning actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges NORMAL. Marlon Brando won Best Actor Oscars for On the Waterfront and The Godfather.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlon Brando, the forename's most famous bearer, won the Best Actor Academy Award on two occasions.

clue.text: Talks at length in 1975 horror movie

definitions.meaning: to jaw is to chat or talk on and on
Steven Spielberg's shark film was released in 1975

explanation.definitionFit: Jawing is long-winded chatter, and the Spielberg shark thriller is the 1975 film of that title.

clue.text: Losing nominees in front of audience snarl so awfully

indicators.note: front of picks out the opening letter of the following word
awfully says the letters of the preceding words are arranged badly into a new order

explanation.surface: Disappointed Oscar candidates growl rudely in view of the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' gives A from 'audience'; 'awfully' rearranges SNARL SO into LSORANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Also-rans are competitors who fail to win or place, as unsuccessful nominees do.

clue.text: Key blokes — they're often thanked in acceptance speeches

definitions.text: they're often thanked in acceptance speeches

parts.note: A is a musical key
gents is an informal word for men or blokes

explanation.surface: Important men are the ones award winners typically thank on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' looks like an adjective meaning important, but it is a musical key, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Film actors' representatives are routinely thanked by winners at awards ceremonies.

clue.text: Actress given a ring by Bogart, initially

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the name it follows

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the telephone

explanation.surface: A screen star receives an engagement ring from Humphrey Bogart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives B from 'Bogart'. Lauren Bacall did in fact marry Bogart, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Lauren Bacall was a Hollywood film star, famous opposite Humphrey Bogart.

clue.text: Protector of many stars' homes in movie of 1984

definitions.text: Protector of many stars' homes in movie of 1984

parts.words: Protector of many stars' homes in movie of 1984
parts.note: a policeman guarding the wealthy Los Angeles district where film stars live, title character of an Eddie Murphy comedy of 1984

explanation.definitionFit: The 1984 Eddie Murphy film is named after a police officer working in the celebrity-filled Los Angeles enclave.

clue.text: Source of Christmas decoration in place of tinsel

definitions.meaning: the evergreen shrub with red berries hung at Christmas, read as its timber
Tinseltown is a nickname for the Los Angeles film district

explanation.surface: Seasonal greenery might be used where tinsel would usually go.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word is a festive shrub's timber; whole, it is the film capital nicknamed Tinseltown.

clue.text: Actor and director in club longing to embrace everyone

parts.note: a wood is a type of golf club

indicators.note: to embrace means the longing word wraps around the everyone word

parts.note: yen is a craving or longing
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A film-maker at a nightclub yearns to hug everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' suggests a nightclub, but here it is a golf club, WOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody Allen both acts in and directs his own films.

clue.text: Absorbed 500 joining British film organisation

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
the Rank Organisation was a major British film company, famous for its gong-man logo

explanation.surface: A large group joins a British film company and is taken in.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rank Organisation was a big British film studio and cinema chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absorbed, such as liquid, has been soaked up or drunk in.

clue.text: Old lady in first part of Eastwood movie

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a grandmother
the opening word of the 2008 Clint Eastwood film ... Torino

explanation.surface: An elderly woman appears early in a Clint Eastwood film.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a familiar name for a grandmother and also opens the title Gran Torino.

clue.text: Winner of special Oscar seen from dress circle

parts.note: garb is clothing or dress
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: An honorary Oscar winner is spotted from the upper tier of a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress circle' is a theatre balcony, but the two words work separately. Greta Garbo received an honorary Academy Award in 1955.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo never won a competitive Oscar but was given an honorary one.

clue.text: In strange way, cameras add what film people strive for

indicators.note: strange signals that the following letters are rearranged into an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: Unusually, cameras contribute to winning film's top honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In strange way' looks like an adverbial phrase; 'strange' rearranges WAY plus CAMERAS ADD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscars, formally the Academy Awards, are the prizes film professionals most hope to win.

clue.text: Check for Oscar material? It's acted badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the preceding letters are arranged poorly into another order

explanation.surface: A critic calls a performance poor when judging whether it deserves an Oscar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges IT'S ACTED. The Oscar statuette is gold-coloured, and acid was once used to test whether metal was genuine gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive trial was originally a test for gold using nitric acid, and Oscar statuettes are gold-plated.

clue.text: Hero of movie -Lord of the Rings?

definitions.meaning: the 2008 Mickey Rourke film is titled after its fighter protagonist
a master of the wrestling ring, not the Tolkien story

explanation.surface: A film protagonist is asked whether he belongs in Tolkien's fantasy epic.
explanation.definitionFit: Mickey Rourke's title character is a grappler, and grapplers rule over the ring where bouts are held.

clue.text: Get all possible advantage from film nominated for Best Picture

definitions.meaning: the 2008 Harvey ... biopic starring Sean Penn was a Best Picture nominee

explanation.surface: Exploit fully a picture up for the top Oscar.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit a situation fully is to drain it like a cow at the pail; the Sean Penn biopic shares the name.

clue.text: With head of studio, rent theatre as place to keep things

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: rent is the past tense of rend, meaning tore
a house is a theatre, as in a full house

explanation.surface: A studio boss hires a theatre for storage space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like hiring, but it is the past of 'rend', TORE; 'head of' gives S from 'studio'.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot for goods is somewhere items are stored.

clue.text: Winner of two Oscars out of touch with reality

definitions.meaning: Kevin ... won for The Usual Suspects and American Beauty
dreamy or vague, as if in outer space

explanation.surface: A double Oscar winner seems detached from the real world.
explanation.definitionFit: Kevin Spacey won two Academy Awards, and the informal adjective means vague or dreamily detached.

clue.text: Directs Helen Mirren in recent role, in elevated circles

indicators.note: in places the queenly letters inside the other piece
elevated in a down entry means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: sets are social circles
Mirren played Elizabeth II in The Queen (2006), and ER is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A film-maker guides Helen Mirren as a monarch among high society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' works because this is a down entry: the circles word is written upwards. Helen Mirren won an Oscar playing Elizabeth II, and ER (Elizabeth Regina) is her royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer is to guide or direct, as a director does a cast.

clue.text: Standard made by top actors and actresses with bands

parts.note: the leading performers are the stars
and means together with
stripes are bands of colour

explanation.surface: A benchmark is set by leading performers accompanied by musical groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' suggests a benchmark, but it is a flag; 'bands' suggests musicians but means stripes.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, and the US flag is known by this name.

clue.text: Moving kind of movie showing in Broadway

indicators.note: showing in tells us the answer can be seen sitting inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A touching film is playing on Broadway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving' suggests touching, but means travelling: a road movie is about a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A road film follows characters on a journey, so it is a genre about travel.

clue.text: This publication is unconnected with mainstream studios, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word for independent films is pronounced, giving a name with the same sound

parts.note: an indie film is made outside the big studios

explanation.surface: This newspaper is said to have no ties with major Hollywood studios.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared in The Independent, whose nickname is the Indy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Independent newspaper, where the puzzle ran, is nicknamed the Indy.

clue.text: Best Actress of 1980 in room with king

parts.note: room means space
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An Oscar-winning actress shares a room with a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Sissy Spacek won Best Actress for Coal Miner's Daughter, a 1980 film.
explanation.definitionFit: Sissy Spacek took the Best Actress Oscar for her role in Coal Miner's Daughter (1980).

clue.text: Don in title role

definitions.meaning: a university lecturer, and a ... is a senior academic rank in British universities
the character named in the 2008 film The ...

explanation.surface: An academic plays the lead role named in a film's title.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities a senior lecturer's rank bears this name, and the 2008 Kate Winslet film is named after one.
